articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan for Future Development Moves Forward
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan, outlining development strategies until 2039, is set for public consultation after council approval. It includes plans for new housing and transport hubs.
articles.content_html:
A plan that will shape Rochdale’s future over the next 13 years has moved closer to implementation following approval from council leaders. The Rochdale Local Plan outlines how the borough will develop until 2039, including the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes to local transport hubs.

The council has refined a 175-page document, which will now enter a public consultation phase. The formal adoption of the plan is anticipated later in 2027. Initially, the plan required that 20 per cent of new housing developments be affordable, but this threshold has been adjusted to 15 per cent due to financial viability concerns. Councillor Daniel Meredith stated that this adjustment does not reflect a reduced commitment to affordable housing, noting that the council has delivered 883 affordable homes in the past five years, exceeding the previous target.

Housing is a central focus of the plan, with designated land for new developments already identified through the Places for Everyone initiative. This strategy, adopted by nine out of ten Greater Manchester councils, aims to construct around 175,000 homes across the region over the next two decades. The Local Plan is expected to attract investment and facilitate major redevelopment in Rochdale, particularly through the Atom Valley scheme, which aims to create 7,000 new homes and 20,000 jobs.

The Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy is a key component of the plan, aiming to transform areas around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy includes enhancements to stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a proposed new station at Slattocks. The plan also incorporates improved walking and cycling routes, park and ride facilities, and community spaces, all intended to boost the local economy and enhance the quality of life for residents.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Central Park Tram Stop
articles.excerpt: The lift at Central Park tram stop towards Rochdale is currently out of service, affecting step-free access for passengers.
articles.content_html:
A lift at Central Park tram stop, which serves passengers travelling towards Rochdale via Oldham, is currently out of service. The disruption began on Wednesday, 29 July, at 5:26pm and will continue until further notice.

Customers travelling towards Oldham can access the Manchester-bound platform via lift from The Gateway and then use the track crossing to reach the Oldham-bound platform. The lift's unavailability may cause inconvenience for those requiring step-free access.

Transport for Greater Manchester has issued an apology for the disruption and is advising passengers to plan their journeys accordingly. For more information, visit the Transport for Greater Manchester website.

articles.title: Rochdale's Local Plan to Shape Future with Thousands of New Homes
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Local Plan, to be discussed on July 28, aims to build nearly 11,000 new homes and transform transport hubs by 2039.
articles.content_html:
A meeting at Rochdale Town Hall on July 28 will discuss the Rochdale Local Plan, which is expected to guide the borough's development until 2039. The plan outlines the construction of nearly 11,000 new homes and significant changes around transport hubs.

The Local Plan is part of a broader strategy, known as the Places for Everyone plan, which aims to deliver around 175,000 homes across Greater Manchester over the next two decades. This initiative is anticipated to attract investment and redevelopment opportunities in Rochdale.

The plan also includes the Rochdale Rail Corridor Strategy, which seeks to enhance areas around transport hubs along the Manchester to Leeds railway line. This strategy aims to create vibrant spaces for living, working, and leisure, focusing on stations in Rochdale, Castleton, Mills Hill, Smithy Bridge, Littleborough, and a proposed new station at Slattocks.

In addition to housing, the Local Plan addresses various topics such as economic growth, climate and energy, and sustainable transport. The town centre is identified as a key area for regeneration, with recent developments including the £20 million restoration of the Grade-I listed Rochdale Town Hall, which is expected to become a significant tourist attraction. The plan will be discussed further at the upcoming council meeting, where it is likely to progress to the next phase before formal adoption.
